metadata.methods_description: EEG data were collected by trained nonspecialist research teams in India and Tanzania over a 30-week period using portable equipment. Daily automated analysis and quality feedback protocols were implemented to maintain data quality standards. Data quality was assessed using PREP and FASTER methods on 5,831 records. The BIDS dataset was generated from EDF source files using MNE-BIDS.

citation_details.title: Electroencephalography (EEG) and the Quest for an Inclusive and Global Neuroscience
citation_details.author: F. Mushtaq, Agustín Ibáñez
citation_details.abstract: The current lack of diversity in neuroimaging datasets limits the potential generalisability of research findings. This situation is also likely to have a downstream impact on our ability to translate fundamental research into effective interventions and treatments for the global population. We propose that electroencephalography (EEG) is viable for delivering truly inclusive and global neuroscience. Over the past two decades, advances in portability, affordability, and computational sophistication have created a tool that can readily reach underrepresented communities and scale across low‐resource contexts—advantages that surpass those of other neuroimaging modalities. However, skepticism persists within the neuroscience community regarding the feasibility of realizing EEG's full potential for studying the brain on a global scale shortly. citation_details.abstract: A large-scale EEG dataset comprising recordings from 7,933 participants across India and Tanzania, collected through field-based research programs with nonspecialist teams. The dataset includes electroencephalographic recordings alongside demographic metadata (age, sex, income) and mental health assessments (Mental Health Quotient scores). Data quality was validated using PREP and FASTER methods and demonstrated comparability to controlled laboratory benchmarks, establishing the feasibility of cost-effective, high-throughput EEG data collection in diverse, low- and middle-income country settings.
